News.title: Terrifying moment out-of-control firework flies into crowd & burns tourists as 27 people injured on Spanish beach
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a firework hurtles into a crowd on a Spanish beach and leaves at least 27 spectators burned.

Shocking footage shows dozens of fireworks exploding overhead, lighting up the night sky with flashes of colour in Alicante.



But one firework veered wildly off course and headed straight towards a packed crowd.

Terrified screams can be heard as it erupts in a huge ball of light, sending sparks into the spectators and burning multiple people.



The terrifying incident unfolded on a beach near Benidorm on Spain’s Costa Blanca.

The fireworks were held to mark the 40th anniversary of the Castell de l’Olla de Altea in the early hours of Sunday.



Around 100,000 people had gathered to watch the spectacular display.

Fourteen people were rushed to hospital following the incident, with 11 treated at the Burns Unit at the General University Hospital of Alicante.

A further 13 people were treated at the Altea Health Centre.

One shaken witness said: “What was supposed to be a night of partying ended in moments of real panic.

“The fireworks went straight towards the area where we were on the beach and people started running.



“Ambulances and emergency services went to the scene. There is talk of numerous wounded.”

The incident was confirmed by the organisers, the Brotherhood of Castell de l’Olla.

They said emergency services – including paramedics – responded quickly to treat and evacuate those affected.

The Castell de l’Olla is a prestigious annual pyrotechnic festival held in Altea, Alicante.

The spectacular display is unique because the fireworks are launched entirely from the sea, using floating platforms and barges.



It comes after crowds were battered by rogue fireworks when a family-friendly display turned into chaos earlier this year.

Onlookers had gathered to watch a fireworks display in Kaohsiung City, Taiwan, when pyrotechnics suddenly began showering the crowd with sparks.

Spectators closest to the explosions recoiled in shock, with some throwing their hands over their faces to protect themselves.

Others were seen scrambling away in panic as deafening bangs rang out and blinding flashes lit up the scene.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Witnesses later described the terrifying scenes as feeling like an “air raid”.



No official injuries were reported following the shocking incident, but several people claimed they had suffered minor burns.

News.title: Chilling moment In-N-Out shooting hero, 17, came face-to-face with gunman & the 4 words he said that saved his life
News.content:
TEENAGE hero Braxton Steube has revealed the heart-pounding moment he stared down the barrel of the gun of the In-N-Out mass shooter.

Three people were killed and seven injured when Chad Williams, 24, opened fire at the newly opened burger restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho, on August 1.



Williams stormed the retail complex armed with a camouflaged AR-15-style rifle, seemingly targeting customers in the drive-thru and firing random shots before fleeing and ending his own life.

Hundreds of people were in the area at the time, Twin Falls police chief Matthew Hicks said at a press conference, as he described the scene as “exceptionally chaotic.”



Heroic citizens raced to help with one armed bystander opening fire at the gunman during the afternoon rampage.

Meanwhile, Steube, 17, who was working at the nearby Dicks Sporting Goods came face-to-face with Williams and describes the moment he distracted him and his life was spared.

“I saw the gun and I just froze and put my hands up and that’s when he pointed the gun directly at me,” the teen told KMVT News.

“I said, I have a family. You don’t have to do this, I’ll tell you whatever you want, I’ll do anything.”

According to Steube, Williams “started to tear up” and said “Just get away from me, man.”

It was this brief conversation and distraction that helped In-N-Out employees evacuate to safety while other heroic bystanders rendered aid to those who were injured.



Chilling footage showed employees scrambling for cover as shots flew through the window into the kitchen.

Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks called the teen a “hero” and said, “your courage, your composure, your selflessness in that moment likely gave others the time they needed to escape harm.”

“This community is grateful for you, and we will never forget what you did that day,” he added.

A motive for the attack has still not been established but Williams was acting alone, police confirmed.



The restaurant reopened on Saturday night “with thoughtful consideration, respect and care,” In-and-Out said in a statement.

“We remain focused on honoring the precious lives lost, supporting those affected, and expressing our gratitude to the many individuals whose courage and compassion brought strength and hope to so many during this incredibly difficult time.

In-N-Out employee Ashley Garibay, 23, from California, was killed when she tried to protect customers.

Christopher Claunch, 59, and Dale Schultz, 66, were also killed in what Hicks described as a “violent, frightening and deeply traumatic” incident.



“It should have been a “normal Saturday afternoon,” he added.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Employees showing up for work. Visitors coming to see our beautiful city. Instead they were confronted with chaos, fear and now loss.”

A joint investigation into the shooting is still ongoing and police have confirmed Williams’ family is cooperating with them.

News.title: Israel rejects Trump’s Board of Peace plan for Gaza as Netanyahu demands ‘full disarmament’ of Hamas before withdrawing
News.content:
BENJAMIN Netanyahu has spurned Donald Trump’s 15-point Board of Peace plan for Gaza.

The Israeli PM vowed that his military will make “no withdrawal” from Palestinian territory until Hamas has fully disarmed.



Netanyahu also warned that there will be no Palestinian state in Gaza or the West Bank for as long as he remains in office.

It comes after Trump claimed last month that there had been a breakthrough in his plan to end the war.



The US president made the bombshell announcement that Hamas had finally agreed to lay down its weapons.

Since the ceasefire agreement came into effect last October, Palestinian officials say around 1,200 people – most women and children – have been killed in Israeli strikes.



During a cabinet meeting on Sunday, Netanyahu said: “Israel rejects the 15-point document.”

He added the Israeli military would “not withdraw at all until Hamas is genuinely disarmed and will continue to thwart threats against our forces and citizens”.

“And when I say disarm Hamas, that means heavy weapons, less-heavy weapons, all weapons. And we are talking about real disarmament, not a fictitious disarmament,” Netanyahu said.

“We are now discussing this with the Americans. They have ideas, some of which are acceptable to us and some are not, and we know how to stand up to those things.”



Trump announced his historic path to disarmament for Hamas and armed groups in Gaza at the end of July.

He also claimed that Hamas’ terror tunnels and infrastructure built since the October 7 massacre in 2023 will be dismantled.

He added: “The agreement will be carried out in carefully structured phases.”



Hamas officials said a committee established by the Board of Peace will help govern Gaza and oversee the process of storing the weapons.

Trump went on to say: “One year ago there was a violent raging war, humanitarian crisis and hostages kept in brutal captivity.

“We have made historic progress and there is still much work to do.

“Congratulations to all on this amazing development that everybody said could never be achieved.”

It came months after he first announced a US-brokered ceasefire between Hamas and Israel.



What happened on October 7? ON October 7 2023, militants of Hamas and other Palestinian nationalist groups launched co-ordinated armed attacks in the Gaza Envelope of southern Israel. The perpetrators had managed to bypass Israeli defences to paraglide across the border, in what became the first invasion of the territory since the 1948 Arab-Israeli War. The horror coincided with the Jewish celebration of Simchat Torah, and initiated the ongoing Israel-Hamas War. A barrage of around 4,300 rockets were launched on Israel from the Gaza Strip in the early hours of October 7 before vehicles and powered paragliders crossed the border. Hamas fighters attacked military bases and massacred civilians in 21 communities, including Be’eri, Kfar Aza, Nir Oz, Netiv Haasara, and Alumim. The first civilian attack started at 6.29am at the Nova Music Festival site at Re’im, just three miles from Gaza. More than 360 revellers were cut down as they desperately tried to flee. Across October 7, an estimated 1,139 people were massacred and another 251 civilians and soldiers were taken hostage into Gaza.

Hamas set it would commit to the terms only if Israel halts its strikes and pulls troops behind the “yellow line,” as defined by the October ceasefire agreement.

Israel currently occupies more than half of Gaza, in the territory’s east and south.

The war in Gaza started over 1,000 days ago after Hamas gunmen stormed the Nova Festival and killed 1,195 people including a 14-hour-old baby and 18 British nationals.

Around 251 people were taken hostage and forced to live in captivity – some for over 500 days.



In response, Israel launched a deadly war which claimed the lives of ten of thousands of Hamas operatives and Palestinian civilians.

Israel launched near daily strikes for almost two years as Netanyahu vowed to kill every last Hamas member to completely eradicate the group.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trump quickly got involved as he returned to the White House in January 2025 as he helped broker a peace deal which took effect on October 10.

Israeli strikes have drastically lessened since the war in Iran plunged the Middle East into further chaos.

News.title: Travellers have invaded our tiny village FIVE times in 9 months – now there are no-go areas… & we’re scared of backlash
News.content:
LIVING IN FEAR Travellers have invaded our tiny village FIVE times in 9 months – now there are no-go areas… & we’re scared of backlash

FUMING locals say five traveller sites have appeared in their tiny village in just nine months, with some claiming they are now too scared to use certain roads.

Residents say the bucolic and peaceful existence in Sandway, Kent, has been ruined and blame the council for not doing enough to tackle the situation.



One resident, who asked to not be named, said: “Obviously we are not happy. It has lowered the value of our houses. It has changed the area. I won’t go down certain roads anymore.”

They added: “Residents don’t want to talk because we live here and we don’t want backlash.



“If I put my name to it they are only down the road so they could come and look into my barn.”

Locals say there are now six unauthorised sites in the immediate area, with another three authorised sites in nearby Lenham Heath.



One site in Warren Lands has been used by travellers for several years.

But residents claim five more sites have appeared within the past nine months.



The latest is near the Wishful Thinker pub and work there began in May.

Residents say they immediately reported the work to Maidstone Borough Council.

But when a council officer visited, they concluded the land had been requested for horse grazing and there had been no breach of planning permission at that stage.

Locals claim that on the next bank holiday weekend a team moved in.

They say several hedges were removed, fresh water pipes installed and a large mobile home brought onto the land.



The landowner has since submitted a retrospective planning application.

But residents say they feel they are being held to a different standard.

Sarah, 35, moved to the village just over a year ago.



She said: “It is just a bit annoying really. They just keep appearing.

“It doesn’t look very nice. Every time I walk down the road I see another one. It doesn’t seem that there is much that can be done.”

She added: “It is frustrating that I have to go through planning permission to paint my door and they can put a stonking great mobile home there and it is all fine.”

A 43-year-old man fears more sites will appear unless the council takes action, claiming they were damaging the area and having a “detrimental effect” on house prices.

He added: “Nobody wants to live here knowing that there could be more travellers moving in.



“They throw foul water out into the streets and they burn big fires. From an environmental point of view, it is very bad. It looks like a scrapyard.”

Another resident, who has lived in the area for 44 years, said: “They need to live somewhere. There aren’t any sites for them to go to, and they aren’t allowed to keep moving.

“It doesn’t bother me. I haven’t seen any problems.”



Lenham Parish Council chairman Cllr John Britt confirmed there were six sites in and around Sandway.

But he said the wider issue was the lack of a clear council policy setting out where Gypsy, Traveller and Showpeople communities could settle.

He said this was unfair to both travelling and settled communities, with the relevant local plan policy missing since the last formal assessment in 2011.

Cllr Britt said the responsibility lay with Maidstone Borough Council as the local planning authority to assess development needs and create a local plan.

A formal complaint has now been lodged by residents calling on the council to act.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Maidstone council spokesman said: “We understand the concerns raised and are investigating both the planning issues and the complaint.

“Officers are currently reviewing all available evidence before determining the most appropriate course of action and it would not be appropriate to comment further while those investigations are ongoing.”

News.title: Tragedy as teen, 19, dies after ‘getting into difficulty’ in lake at popular UK beauty spot
News.content:
LAKE HORROR Tragedy as teen, 19, dies after ‘getting into difficulty’ in lake at popular UK beauty spot

A TEENAGER has tragically died after “getting into difficulty” in a lake at a popular UK beauty spot.

Emergency responders including an air ambulance scrambled to the scene at Grasmere in the Lake District, Cumbria, at around 4.35pm yesterday.

The 19-year-old was rushed to hospital but sadly passed away, and his family have been made aware.

Cops are not treating the death as suspicious but are encouraging anyone who witnessed the incident to get in touch.





A spokesperson for Cumbria Constabulary said: “Emergency services were called at around 4.35pm yesterday (8 Aug) to Grasmere lake following reports that a young man had gotten into difficulty in the water.

“Emergency services including an air ambulance attended and a 19-year-old man was taken to hospital but has subsequently died.

“The teenager’s family have been made aware.

“Whilst the death is not being treated as suspicious, police would encourage anyone who witnessed what occurred to come forward to assist in establishing the circumstances.



“Police would also like to thank those who came to the teenager’s aid, including those who helped get him to shore.”

Anyone with information is urged to report online quoting incident number 201 of 8 August 2026 or call 101.

News.title: Woman, 31, wakes up covered in more than 100 bed bug bites in blood-stained bed after night in Travelodge hotel
News.content:
HOTEL HELL Woman, 31, wakes up covered in more than 100 bed bug bites in blood-stained bed after night in Travelodge hotel

A WOMAN woke up covered in more than 100 bed bug bites in blood-stained sheets after spending a night in a Travelodge Hotel.

Hannah Stephenson, 31, was a guest at the Newmarket Road hotel, Cambridge, when she woke up with itchy red lumps across her body.



Hannah had been out with pals in the city centre and booked a one night stop over in the hotel to save money rather than book a cab home.

But the 31-year-old woke up on July 26 to a “horrible realisation” that she had been bitten over 100 times by bed bugs.



The travel enthusiast told the BBC: “It wasn’t until I saw the blood and the bugs that I realised what had happened,’ she said.

“I woke up feeling itchy and I started to have lumps forming on my arms. When I got up, I saw spots of blood on the pillow and black dots.

“I looked closer and I actually saw a bug on the pillow. I checked the bedding and there were more in the bedding. As the day went on more and more bites started to emerge.

“I counted 37 on my left hand alone but there are too many to count, definitely more than 100, they’re really itchy.”



Hannah said she was “horrified and shocked” by the bites, which she didn’t expect from her stay at the Travelodge as she thought the company was “pretty reliable”.

Her swelling had gone down two weeks later, but she remained feeling “self conscious” as her skin looked as though she was suffering from chicken pox.

Hannah added: “People have been horrified, they’ve said I look like I have a disease. Everyone is saying how bad it looks.”



The 31-year-old said she felt “ignored” when she first complained to Travelodge, and believes the company only contacted her after she posted pictures of the bites on TikTok.

However, Travelodge said they started investigating as soon as the complaint was reported.

According to the British Pest Control Association, bed bugs are not a reflection of cleanliness or hygiene standards and are brought into environments through luggage, clothing and personal belongings.

After living in Asia, Africa and South America without experiencing bed bugs, Hannah said she would “never expect this in Cambridge”.

“I am just hoping these bites will go as soon as possible and I will look normal and get on with my life,” she added.



Hannah has accepted £2,000 in compensation from the hotel but added she hoped the company would take better precautions against bed bugs in future.

A spokesperson for Travelodge said: “We are deeply sorry for Ms Stephenson’s experience and recognise how distressing an incident like this can be.

“The safety of our customers is our priority and we maintain stringent, expert-led measures to prevent and manage pest issues, including training our housekeeping colleagues to be vigilant and to spot early signs wherever possible.

“Bed bug activity affects the wider hospitality sector and is completely unrelated to hygiene or cleanliness standards.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“In the rare instance that an issue is reported in one of our hotels, we immediately take affected and surrounding rooms out of service for inspection and treatment by independent pest control experts.



“We have apologised directly to Ms Stephenson and resolved the matter to her satisfaction.”

News.title: Horror moment thug attacks girlfriend in car during two-year relationship from hell & then laughs as he’s arrested
News.content:
THIS is the moment a thug assaults his girlfriend in the car as she films him, then later laughs at the cops during his arrest.

Footage recorded on his partner’s phone shows Lee Yates, 47, peeling tape off the wingmirror as she tells him to “stop vandalising” her car.



He then orders Daisy (not her real name) to drive, before lashing out and tossing the phone from her grip, saying “do what you want”.

The phone then tumbles into the footwell as Daisy cries out “help me” and repeatedly asks Yates to give the device back.



Further bodycam footage from his subsequent arrest shows him scowling at the officer and crossing his arms defensively.

He then fronts up to the cop and sneers in her face as he denies the allegations.





Further footage, shared with The Sun, also shows him during police interview where he repeatedly says “no comment”.

The vile abuser was jailed at Lewes Crown Court on April 2 after he was found guilty of coercive and controlling behaviour.

For several years, Yates subjected Daisy to a vicious campaign of abuse, from forcing her to cook for him and dictating what she wore, a court heard.

Daisy, from Crawley, West Sussex, said: “He controlled everything in my life, from the time I woke up to the time I went to bed.

“You are scared of them and the easiest thing to do is just to abide by their rules.”



Daisy, 47, met Yates in May 2020 and said that initially he seemed nice but intense, calling her at 3am and sending her reams of messages.

She now realises he’d been love-bombing her – using excessive affection to lure her in.

After a few months had gone by, Daisy began noticing Yates’ darker side – starting with him confiscating her contraceptive pill.

“It was fine for the first four to six months and then it just started creeping up,” she said.

“He started getting angry if I wanted to stay in bed or go out with friends.”



He began controlling her wardrobe, from suggesting she change outift to demanding that she put something else on.

Yates would also time her doing house chores and would even storm in on her if she took more than three minutes in the bathroom.

Daisy said she was forced to make him meals, chauffer him around and give him money for beer.

If she refused, he would allegedly either physically assault her or threaten to kill her pet horses.

She claimed that Yates spat on her, urinated on her and threw things at her on several occasions, as well as attacked her in the car – which she fortunately caught on camera.



Daisy said: “The first time he urinated on me he said ‘I own you now.’

“He put the cold shower on my face and basically burnt my chest.

“It was hell. I physically could not do anymore. You couldn’t say no to him, it wasn’t a word he knew.”

After over two years of torment, the horror finally came to an end, after a neighbour reported Yates shoving Daisy around in the car park.

When cops arrived, Daisy told them about the abuse – realising this could be the only way to escape him.



He was arrested in July and gave a no comment interview.

Daisy said: “I was going to end up dead, I am sure I was.

“The police knocked on the door saying that someone had called. Something in my head went ‘this is your way out’.

Yates was sentenced to three years in prison on April 15 at Lewes Crown Court.

He was also charged with raping her twice but was found not guilty.



Daisy said her diaries provided a useful record of the abuse when giving evidence in court.

She explained how his vile behaviour has had a lasting impact on her and that she still lives in fear, triggered by loud noises or people drinking alcohol.

“When the police arrested him I still felt like I would get in trouble for doing things. Even now there is still stuff that triggers me,” she said.

“I will never be the same again, but I am not letting him win. There is life after trauma.

“I will never let a man treat me like that again.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Speaking after Yates was sentenced Hannah Lane, an investigator at Sussex Police, said: “Lee Yates sought to control almost every aspect of this victim’s life, using violence and intimidation to try and subdue her.

“But he underestimated her strength. Thanks to her reporting his crimes to the police, he is now safely behind bars while she can look to rebuild her life.”

News.title: Amanda Knox’s ex-boyfriend hits out at controversial Edinburgh Fringe comedy show
News.content:
AMANDA Knox’s ex-boyfriend has hit out at her controversial Edinburgh Fringe show.

Raffaele Sollecito, 42, was wrongfully convicted alongside Knox for the 2007 murder of Meredith Kercher in Perugia, Italy, before being acquitted.



He has since joined the line of critics blasting his ex’s show Cartwheel – running for eleven nights at the Gilded Balloon.

A petition launched by a friend of the Kercher family claims that Amanda’s show turns her rape and murder into “entertainment”.



It has since been signed by over 37,000 people.

The computer engineer revealed he was “puzzled” that the murder probe was being used “as a draw for a comedy show.”

He told the Mail on Sunday: “I haven’t seen it, so I cannot pass judgement on its content. However, based on how it has been presented and promoted, I find it puzzling that a tragedy is being used as a draw for a comedy show.

“Personally, it is not an approach I agree with. I am trying to process and move past what happened in a different way.

“I don’t believe there is a right or wrong recipe for dealing with trauma; everyone finds their own path.”

We previously told how Knox, 38, joked about “dry-humping” and dismissed murder trial evidence as “just vibes” in her controversial Fringe debut.



She addressed several moments in the case – including the kiss with Raffaele outside the crime scene.



Knox said: “Even if I had been dry-humping his leg while making awkward eye contact with the lead detective, that would make me in heat, but it wouldn’t have made me a murderer.”

And on her Foxy Knoxy nickname, given to her by school friends and later picked up by the newspapers, she argued: “Even If my nickname were murder pussy, it wouldn’t make me a murderer.”

She added that the cartwheel she was alleged to have done while in police custody was in fact the splits – which is “a lot harder than a cartwheel”.

The murder of Meredith Kercher November 1, 2007 – The murder of Meredith Kercher: British exchange student Meredith Kercher, 21, is found dead in the apartment she shares with Amanda Knox in Perugia, Italy. Her throat is slashed, and signs suggest she may have been sexually assaulted. November 6, 2007 – Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito arrested: Amanda Knox, her Italian boyfriend Raffaele Sollecito, and Patrick Lumumba, Knox’s boss at a local bar, are arrested in connection with Kercher’s murder. Knox accuses Lumumba of the killing during a police interrogation. November 20, 2007 – Patrick Lumumba released: Lumumba is released after police find no forensic evidence linking him to the murder. He was falsely implicated by Knox during a contentious interrogation. December 6, 2007 – Rudy Guede arrested in Germany: Rudy Guede, a 20-year-old Ivorian man, is arrested in Germany and extradited to Italy. His DNA is found on Kercher’s body and at the crime scene. October 28, 2008 – Guede convicted of murder: Guede opts for a fast-track trial and is convicted of Kercher’s murder. He is sentenced to 30 years in prison, later reduced to 16 on appeal. January 16, 2009 – Knox and Sollecito trial begins: Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito stand trial for the murder of Kercher. Prosecutors allege a sex game gone wrong, while the defence argues that Guede acted alone. December 4, 2009 – Knox and Sollecito convicted: Knox and Sollecito are found guilty. Knox is sentenced to 26 years in prison; Sollecito receives 25 years. November 24, 2010 – Appeals process begins: Knox and Sollecito appeal their convictions. A key focus is the forensic evidence, including DNA found on a knife and a bra clasp. October 3, 2011 – Knox and Sollecito acquitted: An appeals court overturns their convictions, citing errors in the forensic investigation. Knox is freed and returns to Seattle. March 26, 2013 – Italy’s Supreme Court orders retrial: Italy’s Court of Cassation annuls the acquittals, ordering a retrial for Knox and Sollecito. January 30, 2014 – Knox and Sollecito reconvicted: Knox and Sollecito are reconvicted in their retrial. Knox, now in the U.S., is sentenced to 28.5 years in prison. March 25, 2015 – Final acquittal: Italy’s Supreme Court definitively acquits Knox and Sollecito of Kercher’s murder, citing lack of evidence and glaring errors in the investigation. November 2021 – Rudy Guede released: Rudy Guede, the sole person definitively convicted in connection with Kercher’s death, is released from prison after serving 13 years. 2023 – present – Knox’s slander conviction: Despite her acquittal, Knox is convicted of slander for falsely accusing Patrick Lumumba. 2023: The European Court of Human Rights rules that Knox’s rights were violated during her 2007 interrogation. June 2024: An Italian court upholds her slander conviction, a decision confirmed by Italy’s high court in January 2025.

Meredith’s sister Stephanie Kercher backed the petition to stop the show and said said she “could not fathom” how rape and murder could be the subject of a comedy gig.



She added: “Imagine 20 years after Meredith’s death, your pain is turned into someone else’s laughter.

“My sister’s tragedy is being used to debut a comedy show this weekend in Edinburgh of all places by the very person who was questioned and taken to the legal system by Italian prosecution.

“I’m very aware that in high profile cases everyone has their own opinions on guilt and innocence and I also agree with freedom of speech.

“However, when someone is still using Meredith’s name to support themselves, and furthermore, when a comedy is linked to an individual case and individual person.

“I cannot fathom how rape and murder can be laughed about and I cannot understand how one person’s behaviour at the police station can be the subject of the comedy show.”



But the Edinburgh Fringe has come to the defence of Knox’s show, saying they are not afraid of controversy.

Tony Lancaster, the director of the Fringe Society, told BBC Radio Scotland: “We’re not afraid of controversy.

“The decision as to whether or not (the show) goes ahead lies with Amanda herself and it lies with the venue.

“Those are conversations that they can have, but as far as I’m concerned, I believe that if you are opening up a stage and calling it an open access festival and inviting people in to tell their stories, you have to be prepared for some controversy – it’s going to happen.

“As sympathetic as we are to individual cases that crop up, and absolutely as a parent, I can relate to the pain that they describe, but that can’t be a criteria, it can’t be one of the lenses that we look through.”



Knox has also previously defended her Fringe show amid the backlash.

She posted to Instagram: “Cartwheel is a show about motherhood, raising a daughter in a world that is unfair and dangerous for women, and what it costs to be the kind of mother who tells her the truth about that.

“Neither the author of this petition nor anyone who signed it has seen Cartwheel.

“The petition contains many false assumptions and completely mischaracterises the show.

“Cartwheel honours Meredith Kercher’s memory and calls out the violence that was done to her and to me.



“A petition to cancel a show no one has seen on the grounds of false accusations intended to shame and vilify a wronged woman into silence is not an argument against Cartwheel.

“It’s a fairly precise description of what Cartwheel is about and why it deserves to exist.

“And the Edinburgh Fringe is the perfect place for a show like this.”

Leeds University exchange student Meredith, 21, from Croydon, South London, was found dead in the flat in Perugia, Umbria, she shared with Knox, now 38.

She had been raped, beaten and had her throat slit.



Knox and then-boyfriend Raffaele Sollecito were convicted of the 2007 killing and sexually assaulting Meredith in what was called a “sex game gone wrong”.

Their convictions were overturned and she received a definitive acquittal in 2015.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

­Ivorian migrant Rudy Guede served 16 years for the crimes.

Knox is now married with two children in the US.

News.title: Andy Burnham to embark on cost of living tour through the UK
News.content:
The prime minister is set to announce "a series of measures to make life easier" for those struggling with the cost of living in the coming days, Downing Street says.

No 10 says Andy Burnham's plans are to "give people some room to breathe". He will also focus on ways of "improving high streets" as he embarks on a tour of the UK.

But the government is facing continued pressure over its early release scheme for prisoners in England and Wales â with criticism of the fact that two of PC Andrew Harper's killers will be eligible from next year.

Burnham is also likely to face pressure for more action on the cost of living â although significant interventions are unlikely before October's Budget.

Even then, Chancellor John Healey has made it clear he will oversee "strong fiscal discipline" â which will limit how much the government has to spend.

The prime minister has been on holiday this week, but Downing Street said he would be in "listening mode" in the coming days as he tours the UK's nations and regions and works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

A spokesman for the prime minister said: "He thinks Westminster has got used to telling people that everyday hassles â like hidden pricing and consumers being ripped off â must be accepted as part of life.

"He doesn't think that's right. That's why he's going to start rolling out a series of pro-consumer cost of living measures to give people some room to breathe."

The spokesman added: "He's also going to be kicking off his summer tour around the country, getting out of Westminster and meeting people where they are.

"The prime minister is going to be in listening mode to help inform his 10-year plan to bring back hope and make Britain better off."

There are, though, likely to be continued questions about the forthcoming early release scheme, due to start in October.

One of Burnham's first acts in Downing Street was to order a review which limited the range of people who would be eligible.

But those convicted of manslaughter will still qualify for the scheme â including two of the killers of PC Andrew Harper.

The prime minister has faced calls from PC Harper's family, former senior police officers and opposition politicians for them to be denied early release.

But he has said he cannot go any further without risking prison capacity. Downing Street said on Saturday night that position remained unchanged, despite reports the prime minister could revisit the case.

News.title: More areas of UK likely to move into drought as fifth heatwave builds
News.content:
Sunday is forecast to be a warmer day across many areas with temperatures widely getting up to the mid to high twenties Celsius. South-east England will be even hotter where temperatures could rise as high as 33C.

After a cooler day on Monday, temperatures will then rise widely across the UK from Tuesday.

In Scotland and Northern Ireland, temperatures will typically reach the low to mid twenties.

In England and Wales, temperatures will rise into the mid to high twenties Celsius and widely across east Wales, central, eastern and southern England in excess of 30C.

The heat is set to peak on Thursday, with readings of 35C possible in south-east England.

If this happens, it will be the fourth consecutive month of 35C or more being recorded.

The threshold for declaring an official heatwave is likely to be reached widely across England and Wales, making it the fifth heatwave of the year for many.

Yellow heat health alerts are in effect for most of England until 21:00 BST on Tuesday, warning of impacts for health and social care services and an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

These are likely to be updated in the coming days as heatwave conditions develop.

News.title: How weight-loss medication is changing relationships with alcohol
News.content:
There is a growing body of research into the link between weight-loss drugs and alcohol consumption.

The drugs, with brands including Wegovy, Mounjaro and Ozempic, contain semaglutide or tirzepatide, which mimic a natural hormone called GLP-1. This suppresses appetite and keeps people feeling fuller for longer, helping them to lose weight.

Early research suggests that because these drugs affect the reward response in the brain, they can reduce cravings for substances including alcohol and nicotine, says Dr Christian Hendershot of the University of South Carolina.

He published a small-scale study, external in 2025 in which participants with alcohol use disorder craved alcohol less while taking Ozempic. Alcohol use disorder, sometimes referred to as alcoholism, is described by the NHS as drinking in a way that is harmful.

A study, external from the University of Colorado Anschutz published last week also suggested that GLP-1 medications in pill form led to fewer days of heavy drinking in people with mild to moderate alcohol use disorder.

People taking the drugs told BBC News that alcohol had affected them in different ways: some said their cravings for it had gone, drinking had made them feel nauseous or uncomfortably full, or they had got drunk more quickly. Others said they had not noticed any effect on their relationship with alcohol.

Before she started taking Wegovy, Lisa says she drank between six and eight bottles of wine a week with friends. But she had sometimes worried about whether this was too much and whether it could damage her health.

NHS guidance, external is that people should not drink more than 14 units a week on a regular basis, which is about six medium glasses of wine or six pints. Drinking too much in the long term can lead to liver damage, high blood pressure and increased risk of cancer.

Lisa says that since starting on the medication she has more than halved her consumption. At a recent day festival, she drank three glasses of wine over the course of nine hours. Previously, she would have had two bottles plus a couple of vodka mixers, she says.

Alcohol has always been a big part of her social life and when she stopped drinking for a few weeks in the late 2010s, she realised friends had stopped inviting her to social events. It led her to start drinking again.

This time round, Lisa says that she still looks forward to drinking wine, but after having a couple of glasses she simply cannot stomach any more.

"I still feel involved in things because I'm still drinking but drinking a lot less," Lisa says.

For years, Warren Thomas, 45, from Colchester, had enjoyed an occasional beer with his family after work, as well as one or two heavy drinking sessions with his friends each month.

But when he spoke to his friends on weight-loss medication about his plans to start taking Mounjaro, they warned him that it could affect how much he drank.

Warren says he noticed the effect within 24 hours of his first dose in mid-June. "I just don't want to drink," he says. "I've just got no appetite for it."

When he went out for his friend's birthday last month, he felt "light-headed and a little bit giddy" after two beers, he says.

"My tolerance level to drinking is now zero," he says.

There is no formal advice in the British National Formulary, a guide to dispensing medicine used by doctors and pharmacists, about whether people on weight-loss drugs should stop drinking alcohol, says Prof Russell Hearn, a GP and professor of medicine at King's College London.

But he gives careful advice to his patients. "Alcohol has a lot of calories in it and if your goal is to lose weight, drinking less will definitely help you with that alongside changing your diet while you're on a GLP-1," he says.

For people like Lisa and Warren, drinking less alcohol has been a happy bonus. But recent graduate Faye Goodwin, 20, feels that it has hampered her social life.

When Faye drinks she says she gets nauseous very quickly and sometimes throws up or gets bad acid reflux.

Faye, who got in touch with BBC Your Voice, has been taking Mounjaro since she was 18 and does not really know what it is like to drink alcohol without the impact of weight-loss medication. But she says she once took a month off the jabs and was able to drink without experiencing any nausea.

News.title: Killed a month after his wedding - why PC Andrew Harper's story touched so many
News.content:
On the night of 15 August 2019, Lissie Harper got a knock at the door. She thought it was her husband Andrew coming home from work.

Instead, it was uniformed officers, there to tell her that the man she had married four weeks earlier had been killed while on police duty.

"Everything I had known in my life to be true was robbed away. Every ounce of beautiful peace, gone," Lissie later said of the moment she was told.

They had met as teenagers and were together for 13 years.

In her eulogy at his funeral, Lissie recalled how Andrew would pass her notes in class.

They were, she said, "true childhood sweethearts, loving one another more and more with each passing day".

They had been about to go on their honeymoon.

But, on that night nearly seven years ago, everything changed.

The case has been back in the headlines because two of PC Harper's killers â Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole â will become eligible to be released early under government plans to tackle prison overcrowding.

As the disturbing details of the case are revisited, his family, fellow officers and the public are outraged once more â at what happened, and at the perpetrators' impending release.

PC Harper's death was brutal and devastating, causing shock, anger and an outpouring of grief across the country.

Pictures of the smiling faces of his teenage killers laughing and joking as they left court only added to that anger.

PC Harper had been about to head home at the end of a long shift when he and a colleague were called to reports of a burglary.

He was "going beyond the call of duty", the prosecutor at the Old Bailey trial in 2020 said.

During the case, haunting dashcam footage from the police patrol car was played showing the moment PC Harper confronted teenagers Henry Long, Bowers and Cole down a dark country lane. He then disappeared from view.

His ankles had got caught in a strap trailing behind the car being driven by Long that had been used to tow a stolen quad bike.

PC Harper was dragged for over a mile. He died on the road. His police badge and stab vest were found scattered along the route.

The three teenagers were tried for murder. In the end, the jury convicted Bowers and Cole of manslaughter. Long had already pleaded guilty to that offence.

It meant the jury was not sure that PC Harper's killers knew they were dragging the officer behind the car.

But the Judge, Mr Justice Edis, described it as a manslaughter case which was "very close to a case of murder" in its seriousness.

News.title: Australia is the planet's extinction hotspot, but one animal offers a glimmer of hope
News.content:
"Eyes peeled," comes the order from the front passenger seat.

Obediently, we scan the ends and tops of logs, looking between low scrub and patches of vivid wildflowers for a flash of stripes or a dart of movement.

Eluding us is the numbat, a rare Australian marsupial which could be the love-child of a chipmunk and an anteater.

Numbats were once populous across the bottom half of the continent, but Dryandra Woodland â in the south-western corner of Australia â is one of the few places they remain.

As we slowly roll along bush tracks, researchers explain how this annual trip helps plot the species' survival.

Classified as endangered until this month, numbats have been bouncing back. This team's efforts have seen them scratched off the international red list of threatened species - a rare glimmer of hope in a country facing an extinction emergency.

This part of Australia is the front line of that crisis: a last stand for many species driven to the brink by feral pests, disease, urban development, habitat destruction and climate change.

Winging over our car at one point is the endangered Carnaby's cockatoo. On an island just off the coast is one of the last surviving pockets of the world's rarest marsupial, the Gilbert's potoroo. Diving in the sapphire waters around it is the increasingly scarce Australian sea lion.

News.title: Zendaya saw me on the red carpet and her jaw dropped - I'm still in shock
News.content:
"I can't zip this! Mummm?"

This was 29-year-old Zainab Jiwa, calling out for help squeezing into a corset while filming a "get-ready-with-me" TikTok video. It's a scene many 20-somethings still living at home will relate to.

The difference is, Zainab was on her way to the recent London premiere of The Odyssey, one of the summer's biggest blockbusters.

She was invited there as a guest and says she caught the eye of Hollywood megastar Zendaya, thanks to her custom look: a striking gold gown complete with a hood.

"She just walked past, and she saw me there. Her jaw just dropped, so did mine," Zainab tells me.

"It was just a stare-off for a minute, and she was like, 'Oh my god, amazing, amazing,' and then she just walked off."

"Iâm still in shock,â she adds. âThe thought of her noticing my outfit blew my mind."

The interaction went viral, external with 19m TikTok views. Her phone blew up.

While Zendaya has been ruling the red carpets with high-fashion "method dressing" â where stars match outfits to a film's themes â Zainab is perhaps proving that independent creators like her can give Hollywood a run for its money.

Zainab, who is Muslim and wears a hijab, is also often one of the only people covering her hair at premieres, but she says finding ways to incorporate modest wear is part of the fun.

"Even though you're covered, you can still find a way to be on theme.â

News.title: Why eclipse chasers are crossing continents for solar spectacle: 'It's like the World Cup'
News.content:
On Wednesday, parts of Europe will be plunged into daytime darkness as the moon passes in front of the sun, temporarily blocking its light and casting a shadow across the continent.

For many of us, it will be a once-in-a-lifetime experience. But for some, following eclipses has become something of an addiction.

Armed with two high-spec cameras, a specialist telescope and a drone, Mark Griffiths has spent two days driving from Cheshire to Galicia - one of the best places to view the eclipse - to record the event.

It's a hobby that started six years ago, when he went to Shetland to see the northern lights - though the weather was so dreary he "didn't see anything".

But it didn't put him off and he soon found he couldn't stop. He loved the thrill of witnessing and capturing the sky's most spectacular events.

News.title: Hundreds arrested over French wildfires, but who is to blame?
News.content:
After wildfires caused more damage in France this year than at any time since World War Two, many are left asking a single question: Why?

A major driver is that climate is changing as a result of the well-documented way humanity is burning fossil fuels. Temperatures are only rising.

But with records showing that nine out of 10 French wildfires are started by humans, the government in Paris is trying to attribute blame - although it is itself accused of being underprepared for the infernos that have now scorched more than 300,000 acres this summer.

The interior ministry has announced 420 arrests of people alleged to have either started the fires deliberately or by accident. Among them are 166 minors.

In one case, a 23-year-old man has been accused of deliberately starting 10 fires in the space of five days in the south-eastern Var area last month. He faces 15 years in prison and a â¬150,000 (Â£128,000) fine, if convicted.

Many others have been tried and immediately sentenced, such as a man who received a three-year jail sentence for starting three recent fires in the Raon-L'Ãtape forest in the Vosges region.

"Only a few square metres of vegetation went up in smoke," noted L'Est RÃ©publicain, the newspaper that reported the story.

Other prosecutions have been perceived as heavy-handed and unjust. A homeless man and someone with severe autism have reportedly been handed jail terms for throwing cigarette butts.

"I was amazed at the number of arrests, it feels excessive," admits Muriel Gestas, a lawyer who has represented several people accused of arson, including two firefighters. She doubts many will lead to a conviction.

The newspaper Le Monde is also unconvinced. It questions to what extent police have examined these cases, given the short time frame.

The authorities' silence on the details - the specific charges, notably whether they involve intent and how the numbers compare with past seasons - rules out any meaningful comparison with previous years, it argues.

But Bordeaux prosecutor Renaud Gaudeul told Le Monde that a tough approach was justified by current circumstances.

"The conditions for a charge of endangering lives are met for those who throw a cigarette butt or light a barbecue in wooded areas. It only takes a tiny spark for it to start," the newspaper quoted him as saying.

News.title: Family 'devastated' as hit-and-run driver who killed boy, 13, to have early prison release
News.content:
The family of a 13-year-old boy killed in a hit-and-run say they are "devastated" after being told the driver who caused his death has had his sentence reduced.

Kaylan Hippsley died three days after being struck by a car driven by Harley Whiteman on Brecon Road in Hirwaun, Rhondda Cynon Taf, on 29 February 2024.

Whiteman was originally sentenced to six years and nine months in prison and banned from driving for eight years and four months but, after Kaylan's family appealed, High Court judges increased the sentence to nine years.

Now, the family has been told Whiteman can be released under licence as early as this autumn as part of the UK government's Sentencing Act early release scheme.

News.title: Kellie Bright to leave EastEnders after 13 years
News.content:
EastEnders star Kellie Bright is to leave the soap after playing one of its key characters, Linda Carter, for 13 years.

She arrived in Albert Square with on-screen husband Mick, portrayed by Danny Dyer, when they became the new owners of the Queen Vic pub.

Carter's matriarch character has been central to major storylines including plots about murder, sexual assault and alcoholism.

Bright said she made the "tough decision" to leave more than a year ago but "happily" agreed to stay on to be part of an "exciting storyline".

The BBC has promised "unmissable drama" before her on-screen exit, which is said to be a "while away" yet.

Executive producer Ben Wadey described the actor as being "the beating heart of EastEnders" and said she had become "a classic EastEnders icon".

Viewers have seen the much-loved character at the heart of many emotional storylines including in 2014 when she was raped by her brother-in-law Dean Wicks.

More than 7 million people watched the episode which prompted dozens of complaints. The sexual assault led to long-running story arc about family conflict and trauma.

News.title: Rare turtle to be sent back home in 5,000-mile 'incredibly emotional' trip
News.content:
It has taken almost two years to plan, including building a special temperature-controlled crate for him, and co-ordinating complex paperwork across two countries.

Rhossi normally lives in the sea, but has to travel out of the water â first by helicopter from Anglesey to London, then by cargo flight to Houston, Texas, USA.

It means the journey needs to be completed as quickly as possible, and staff have to be constantly on hand to make sure he does not dry out or dehydrate.

Davidson said: "We have to make sure that the shell is really well lubricated, so we spread Vaseline all over to stop it drying out and flaking off.

"The same for the skin â it's really delicate â and especially the eyes, which both have to be lubricated before he goes into the crate and again just before takeoff, or he will start to peel like someone getting sunburned.

"But I have had to go to the checkout in a chemist's with about eight tubes of KY Jelly and three tubs of Vaseline and explain what's happening when I get strange looks."

News.title: Hot weather reveals hidden history across the South
News.content:
As the south of England continues to enjoy an unusually warm and dry summer, parch marks on lawns across the region have revealed the hidden histories of their location.

Among the sites which have seen the outlines of historic installations exposed by the hot weather are Portchester Castle and Blenheim Palace.

At Blenheim, the footprint of an 18th century garden - which had once stretched across the width of the entire palace - has revealed itself on a lawn.

Andy Mills, the Unesco World Heritage Site's head gardener, told the BBC it was "absolutely magical" to see the outlines of the historic parterre - 260 years after it was demolished.

Mills explained that the original parterre - which is a French word meaning 'on the ground' - had been constructed in 1705, and would have "cost an absolute fortune to install".

"It was a very large extravagant thing to do, but it was a way of showing your wealth and importance and that sort of thing," he said.

News.title: Attempted murder arrest after three hit by car
News.content:
A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and dangerous driving after three pedestrians were hit by a car following reports of a disturbance.

The incident happened on Stokes Croft in Bristol at about 06:30 BST, according to Avon and Somerset Police.

A spokesperson for the force said one of the pedestrians was taken to hospital, but their injuries were "not believed to be as serious as initially thought". The two others were not seriously injured.

A man police believe to be the car's driver was treated for facial injuries after his arrest.

Thomas Street, Hepburn Road, Stokes Croft and City Road are all closed while police make enquiries, with more officers than usual in the area as investigations continue.

The Best Off Licence in Stokes Croft was also damaged in the incident.

Bristol Supt Matt Ebbs said: "We would like to assure the public we do not believe there to be any wider threat.

"Anybody with concerns is welcome to speak to officers on the ground, but we would also appeal to anybody with CCTV, dashcam or mobile phone footage which may assist our enquiries to contact us."

News.title: Banksy works cost public almost £150,000
News.content:
Three artworks by street artist Banksy have cost taxpayers almost Â£150,000 in cleaning operations and security so far, with the bill expected to rise.

The largest single cost relates to a mural painted on the Royal Courts of Justice in September 2025, where removal efforts and security have so far cost more than Â£85,000.

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) says it has spent Â£50,000 trying to remove paint from the wall of the Grade II-listed building in Carey Street. A further Â£35,300 was spent on overtime and security costs.

The spending was disclosed to the BBC through Freedom of Information requests and is likely to reignite debate over whether Banksy's work is vandalism or valuable public art.

News.title: Stray cats showing up at raves, gigs and pubs now have own merchandise
News.content:
Celebs pulling in punters with a club appearance is nothing new. But did they ever have so much fur?

At venues in Coventry at least, the glitterati wear whiskers these days.

It began when two stray cats made city venues their home, becoming social media stars thanks to the incongruous sights of tail and turntable, pint and paw.

While one shows up at gigs and rave nights, the other is a bit more pub than dub. But each now has his own range of merch... and visitors flock for a glimpse of these meeow-vers and shakers.

Murphy was first spotted living beneath a bush before wandering into the car park of The Old Windmill pub in the city centre, "rake thin" and in need of care.

Now a permanent resident, he has become a firm favourite with customers.

"We've had people who've never been in the pub before, but have seen him on social media," said the venue's Peter Dunkley. "They come in and the first question is 'where's Murphy'?"

Across town, Fargo is a well-known figure at Fargo Village, the creative hub after which he is named.

Regularly spotted around the site's shops and bars, he too has become an attraction in his own right, mixing among ravers and drinkers.

Fargo Village staff have set up an Instagram account in an effort to track down his owner, and it has attracted a loyal following of fans eager to keep up with his daily adventures.

News.title: Man's body found in burning car
News.content:
The body of a man has been found inside a burning car in Portadown, County Armagh.

Police were called to the scene at Harford Street in the town centre at about 22:00 BST on Saturday.

Firefighters extinguished the blaze and the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

Ch Insp Tierney, from the Police Service of Northern Ireland said the circumstances are under investigation and a post-mortem examination will be carried out to determine the cause of his death.

The cause of the car fire will also be investigated.

The vehicle's windows were smashed and it was significantly damaged by the blaze.

A neighbouring property in the street sustained scorch damage, according to police.

The officer added: "Ammunition Technical Officers (ATO) were also tasked to the scene to conduct relevant enquiries â we can confirm there is no risk to the public."

Myanmar’s military-backed government has rejected the Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ (Asean) renewed call for the unconditional release of detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi and dismissed the need for the organisation’s special envoy on Myanmar, according to the foreign affairs ministry.

President Min Aung Hlaing, the former army chief who had originally seized power in 2021 from Suu Kyi’s civilian government, has been trying to win political legitimacy since the takeover and resume relations with Asean.

Asean came up with a peace plan for the Southeast Asian country in April 2021 to end hostilities and initiate dialogue among contending parties, to be facilitated by the special envoy. Mr Min has since been barred from attending top-level meetings for failing to comply with the plan.

In an apparent effort to placate critics, the government allowed a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross to visit 81-year-old Ms Suu Kyi last week, the first known contact with an outside international independent humanitarian organization since her detention five years ago.

Ms Suu Kyi is serving her sentence under house arrest at an undisclosed location in the capital Naypyitaw, on charges that her supporters and rights groups have said are politically motivated.

Myanmar's ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi, left, shakes hands with Arnaud de Baecque, resident representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross ( AP )

The current Asean chair, the Philippines, welcomed the meeting as a step toward dialogue and reconciliation on Friday, while urging greater access to political detainees and reiterating its call for Ms Suu Kyi’s “complete and unconditional release.”

Myanmar’s foreign ministry's statement late on Saturday criticised the call.

“Although the government has commuted her sentences based on humanitarian considerations, the matter of a full and unconditional release shall only be carried out in accordance with the law,” it said.

The statement also said the government will continue working with Asean’s current special envoy, Philippine foreign minister Maria Theresa Lazaro, but doesn’t see the need to continue down that path when Singapore takes over on 1 January 2027.

“At present, the government, which emerged from the multiparty democratic elections reflecting the genuine will of the people, has assumed state responsibility,” the statement said.

In a speech more than three months after being sworn in as president following the elections, Mr Min dismissed Asean’s peace plan, saying some member states have discriminated against Myanmar and it would respond on a case-by-case basis.

Critics dismissed the elections, which were held in December and January, as a sham designed to consolidate the military’s grip on power while ostensibly restoring civilian rule.

News.title: Arsenal v Borussia Dortmund LIVE: Gunners fall behind early in Emirates Cup clash after Guimaraes unveiled
News.content:
Why Arsenal Want Bruno Guimaraes So Badly

Arsenal bid to step up their pre-season preparations as the Premier League champions take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup.

The Gunners have has been boosted by the signing of Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes this week and although the midfielder is set to be presented to the Emirates ahead of kick-off after completing his £75m move, Arsenal fans will have to wait a little longer to see his debut.

Arsenal are still without some of their World Cup stars, such as England’s Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka, but Gabriel Magalhaes made his comeback in Wednesday’s 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin as Mikel Arteta’s squad slowly returns to full strength.

There are now less than two weeks before Arsenal face FA Cup winners Manchester City in the Community Shield, with Arteta’s side beginning their Premier League title defence at home to Championship winners Coventry on Friday 21 August.

Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected Donald Trump's Gaza peace plan, insisting Israel will not withdraw until Hamas fully disarms.

The US president claimed last month that there had been a breakthrough in his plan to end the war, which both Israel and Hamas agreed to last year and which started with the ceasefire.

Trump said that Hamas, which ruled Gaza for nearly two decades before ‌carrying out the October ​7, 2023 ‌attack on Israel that ⁠triggered the Gaza ⁠war, had agreed to lay ‌down ​its weapons.

"Israel rejects the 15-point document," Netanyahu said at a cabinet meeting on Sunday, as reported by the BBC.

The Israeli military "will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed and will continue to thwart threats against our forces and our citizens", he added.

The Israeli prime minister added he is now discussing with US officials about how to go forward, deeming some ideas “acceptable” while some “are not”.

open image in gallery Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected Donald Trump's Gaza peace plan ( Reuters )

Last month, Egypt, which is mediating discussions between Israel and Hamas, said that both sides had agreed to a new 15-point roadmap and that a future meeting would be held in Cairo “to discuss implementation mechanisms”.

Trump had thanked Egypt, Qatar and Turkey for mediating the agreement and called the deal “historic”.

A senior Hamas negotiator said at the time that the group’s disarmament is conditional on Israel fulfilling its commitments under the agreement, including withdrawing from Gaza and allowing the establishment of a national committee and reconstruction efforts.

Senior Hamas official Ghazi Hamad said: “The agreement contains a clear provision stating that Israel must commit to and implement its obligations. If Israel does not implement the agreement, neither will we.”

open image in gallery Gaza has been reduced to rubble after Israel’s relentless attacks of the strip ( Reuters )

Israel’s rejection of the plan is a further block for Trump who announced his Gaza peace plan in September last year.

Just months away from Israeli elections, Netanyahu is unlikely to pull back from his hardline stance.

Last month, Netanyahu told his cabinet that he would not agree to requests from the US to withdraw troops from locations in Syria, Lebanon, and Gaza, according to Channel 13.

Sources told the broadcaster that Netanyahu said he would “stand on my own two feet and resist” amid growing pressure from the Israeli far-right for the military campaign to continue.

What is in Trump's 15-point plan for peace in Gaza?

The deal included the total disarmament ‌of Hamas and other groups in Gaza as well as the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the territory.

It also stipulates that Hamas and ‘other factions’ agree that “all civilian governance and security functions in Gaza shall be handed over” to a new technocratic body set up to run the enclave.

With that, the technocratic body will take over responsibility for handling “internal security incidents.”

The 15-point plan also says that that process will be “linked” to an Israeli withdrawal “in phases”, towards a complete withdrawal from the Palestinian enclave. There is no mention of a reconstruction process.

open image in gallery The Israeli PM is unlikely to pull back from his hardline stance ahead of the country’s elections ( GPO )

Under the initial deal to end the war, Israel was supposed to pull back to a demarcation termed the Yellow Line, separating 47 per cent of the land controlled by the Palestinians from the 53 per cent controlled by Israel. Israel was supposed to steadily withdraw from its position, but has instead increased its area of control to around two-thirds.

The Board of Peace on Monday had hailed a “constructive and detailed” meeting between Netanyahu, Israeli officials and Gaza envoy Nikolay Mladenov.

The Board noted that the full withdrawal of the Israeli military beyond the Yellow Line “will take place only once decommissioning is complete, as Hamas committed to the mediators”.

Hamas rejects the word “disarmament” but has said it will hand over its weapons for storage under the control of a US-backed Palestinian administration after Israel halts operations and withdraws its forces in line with last year's ceasefire.

A conflict continues to surround the order in which Hamas and Israel implement their respective de-escalations.

News.content:

Arsenal have moved on from their chase of Vinicius Jr after he signed a contract extension with Real Madrid and the Gunners have now reignited their interest in Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez, while PSG’s Bradley Barcola is also on their list.

Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected Donald Trump’s 15-point peace plan for Gaza, saying Israel will not withdraw from the enclave until Hamas fully disarms.

At a cabinet meeting on Sunday, Israel’s president said it "will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed and will continue to thwart threats against our forces and our citizens”, the BBC reported.

He insisted that any disarmament by the militant group, which ran Gaza for nearly two decades before ‌carrying out the October ​7, 2023 ‌attack on Israel that ⁠triggered the Gaza ⁠war, must not be a “fictitious” one.

Mr Netanyahu said he was in discussions with US officials about how to proceed. “They have ideas; some of them are acceptable to us and some are not, and we know how to stand our ground on these matters,” he said.

What is Trump’s 15-point plan for peace in Gaza?

Last month, Donald Trump’s “Board of Peace” in Gaza published a “roadmap” for implementing a “comprehensive peace process” between Israel and Hamas, nearly 10 months since both sides agreed to terms to stop the fighting.

The US president hailed the agreement as a “major milestone” in the peace process, saying the deal included the total disarmament ‌of Hamas and other groups in Gaza as well as the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the territory.

The roadmap says that Hamas and ‘other factions’ agree that “all civilian governance and security functions in Gaza shall be handed over” to a new technocratic body set up to run the enclave.

open image in gallery Despite the agreement to end the war, Palestinians were left sifting through rubble on Thursday following an air strike in the Al-Nasr neighborhood of western Gaza City ( AFP/Getty )

With that, the technocratic body will take over responsibility for handling “internal security incidents.”

The 15-point plan also says that that process will be “linked” to an Israeli withdrawal “in phases”, towards a complete withdrawal from the Palestinian enclave. There is no mention of a reconstruction process.

But Hamas has said it would only comply with the directive once Israel withdraws from Palestinian territory and stops its attacks in Gaza.

Here’s what the ‘roadmap’ says in full:

open image in gallery Hamas said it would give up its weapons once Israel fulfills its commitments (file, 2012) ( Reuters )

Principles:

1. All parties reaffirm their commitment to President Trump’s Comprehensive Plan to achieve peace in Gaza, which constitutes, together with the UN Security Council Resolution no. 2803 (2025), the agreed upon international framework guiding the implementation of this process.

Through this process, the parties aim at ending the cycle of destruction, securing the complete Israeli withdrawal from Gaza Strip, restoring normal life, enabling Palestinian governance, reconstruction, security, recovery and economic development, rehabilitating damaged sectors and facilitate launching a credible political path that achieves self-determination and Statehood.

2. Israel shall fully complete, without delay, all remaining commitments under Sharm Sheikh Protocol, particularly the cessation of military operations as detailed in annex (1).

Hamas and the Palestinian factions shall complete the cessation of all military operations in accordance with Sharm Sheikh Protocol and the Peace Plan. In parallel, the timetable and implementation mechanisms of this Roadmap (“Implementation of Phase 2”) shall be prepared within 14 days after all parties approve the Roadmap, which could be extended by a decision by the International Verification Committee (IVC). Upon the completion of the timetable and implementation mechanisms, the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) shall enter the Strip and start to assume its responsibilities. The IVC, that shall be established by the Board of Peace (BoP), comprising representatives from the guarantors, BoP and the International Stabilization Force (ISF), shall certify that both parties fulfill their commitments under the Roadmap before proceeding to the implementation of Phase 2.

3. Progression from one phase to the following one shall be contingent on the verified completion of the commitments of the previous phase. This verification shall be done by the IVC, which shall also observe any violations by either party through an enhanced monitoring mechanism.

open image in gallery Hamas demands that Israel leave the Palestinian enclave and end its strikes (28 July pictured) ( AP )

4. Hamas and other factions agree that all civilian governance and security functions in Gaza shall be handed over to NCAG in accordance with President Trump’s Comprehensive Peace Plan in Gaza. They also assert that NCAG shall enjoy full independence in carrying out its responsibilities and that the factions shall not interfere in NCAG affairs during the transitional period, in accordance with UNSC Resolution 2803 (2025).

5. Upon fully assuming its responsibilities in Gaza, NCAG shall maintain the continuity of civilian institutions and public services.

All civil servants shall be treated lawfully, fairly and with dignity with respect to their rights. Those whose services are terminated or who are retired during the transitional period shall receive their rights in accordance with the Palestinian law.

With international support, NCAG shall carry out a comprehensive audit of the financial and administrative affairs in Gaza, and protect, recover and administer public assets and resources.

NCAG shall seek to assess the legitimate commitments to suppliers, contractors and other parties – up to a total amount of no more than $400M USD - and address them.

The implementation of these measures will be undertaken gradually, within three years, in accordance with priorities determined by the NCAG.

Any unresolved financial rights, liabilities or claims shall be addressed within the context of a wider national process later, and in accordance with the relevant Palestinian law.

open image in gallery Donald Trump announced the disarmament agreement, discussed last year, on Truth Social on Thursday ( Getty )

Security:

6. Gaza shall be governed according to the principle of One Authority, One Law, One Weapon. NCAG shall operate in accordance with Palestinian laws, relevant international standards and the principles of good governance.

7. Newly-trained police personnel shall be incorporated into existing police structures. All police personnel shall undergo a comprehensive vetting. Those who do not meet the required standards of vetting shall be offered alternative civilian roles consistent with their earlier experience or retire in accordance with the Palestinian law. None of those shall be deprived of their financial rights, particularly due to political affiliation. All police weapons shall be transferred to the responsibility and authority of NCAG upon its entry into Gaza and the assumption of its missions.

8. A process to decommission and store heavy weapons, military production sites, depots of weapons, and tunnels, shall begin after completing the remaining commitments under Sharm Sheikh Protocol, the entry of NCAG and deployment of ISF.

This process shall be administered and implemented by NCAG in a gradual, sequential and time-bound manner according to an implementation timetable that shall be completed within 14 days after all parties approve the Roadmap, which could be extended by a decision by IVC.

This process shall be linked to an Israeli withdrawal, in phases, from the areas under its control in Gaza and the decommissioning of armed militias in accordance with article 10 of this Roadmap.

open image in gallery Palestinian children search among clothing and household belongings scattered across the rubble after an Israeli airstrike in the Al-Nasr ( AFP/Getty )

This process shall be monitored and verified by IVC and supported by ISF.

The Palestinian factions shall take part in this process, and no weapons shall be transferred or handed to Israel or non-Palestinian parties.

At the end of the process mentioned in articles 7 – 10 of this Roadmap, only NCAG shall hold, store or control weapons in Gaza.

The implementation of this Roadmap, including the issue of weapons and other articles of the comprehensive peace plan, shall create appropriate conditions for a credible pathway towards achieving Palestinian self-determination and statehood.

9. Personal weapons in Gaza shall be subject to the regulations of relevant Palestinian laws. As the transitional authority in the Strip, NCAG shall be the sole authority to register weapons, issue and revoke licenses and enforce the law, including through reintegration and social support. All factions, clans and components of the Palestinian society in Gaza shall cooperate with NCAG in this process.

open image in gallery An Israeli Merkava main battle tank moves at a position along the border with the Gaza Strip on June 5, 2025 ( AFP/Getty )

10. Weapons of the militias shall be decommissioned and stored under NCAG authority according to an agreed upon timetable. Members of those militias shall not be integrated in the security and police services. IVC shall be responsible for certifying the implementation of this issue.

11. A Social Peace Agreement shall be signed in accordance with Palestinian norms and laws. It shall include commitments to immediately end internal violence, avoid reprisals, shows of force, military parades and armed demonstrations.

International Stabilization Force (ISF) and withdrawal of Israeli forces:

12. The temporary International Stabilization Force (ISF) shall be deployed in Gaza Strip to separate the Israeli forces from NCAG-controlled areas. ISF shall not perform any police mission or missions related to the Palestinian society. Furthermore, it shall monitor compliance by all parties with the ceasefire, train the Palestinian police, secure the protection and delivery of humanitarian assistance and essential supplies into Gaza Strip, and support the NCAG, at its request, in any other non-policing mission.

13. Israeli forces shall complete their phased withdrawal from Gaza Strip according to an agreed upon timetable, consistent with article “8” of the Roadmap and in accordance with President Trump’s Comprehensive Peace Plan, which includes a commitment not to force anyone to leave the Strip.

14. NCAG shall be responsible for handling internal security incidents.

Reconstruction:

15. Implementation of the reconstruction of Gaza Strip and the provision of necessary resources and financing shall take place according to a plan and timetable prepared and supervised by BoP and NCAG in accordance with relevant laws and international standards.

News.title: Irish ‘gangland crime boss’ Daniel Kinahan extradited from Dubai: ‘I’m looking forward to getting back home’
News.content:
