Suspected Irish crime gang boss Daniel Kinahan has been handed over to authorities from his home country after being extradited from the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

Kinahan, who was ‌arrested in ‌Dubai in April, was named ⁠as one of three leaders of the Kinahan organised crime group by the United ‌States in ​2022 when ‌it ⁠offered a $5m ⁠reward for their ‌arrest.

He was also identified in the High Court in Dublin as a senior figure who “controlled and managed” the operations of the organised crime group.

Reacting to news of his planned extradition, Kinahan said that he was “looking forward to getting back home”.

His extradition, reported by UAE state media on Sunday, comes after several months of preparations, in what is said to be one of the biggest security operations the Irish government has ever launched, following the arrest of the Dublin boxing promoter in April.

Kinahan, aged in his late 40s, was detained on foot in April after an arrest warrant was issued by the Irish courts in relation to alleged serious organised crime, including drug and firearms offences.

An Irish government jet took off from Casement aerodrome in Baldonnel on the outskirts of Dublin on Saturday morning. It departed ‌for Ireland ​at 09.20 GMT on Sunday, ‌flight tracking data showed.

Kinahan, who has lived openly in Dubai for 10 years, will be arrested on arrival in Ireland, following years of investigations by the Garda Drugs ‌and Organised Crime Bureau, the Irish Times reported.

He is expected to face a charge of directing organised crime when he appears before the Special Criminal Court in Dublin on Sunday night, the newspaper added.

Snipers on roofs, bomb-proof vans for transportation, decoy vans and signal jammers in prison ceilings will be deployed to bring Kinahan to trial,The Times reports.

Kinahan spoke about the process on Saturday, leaving a voice message that was shared on Instagram by podcaster James English, in which he said that he was “looking forward to getting back home”.

He said: “The security is going to be crazy. I am sitting here reflecting a little.

“Then I’m thinking of what happened, how I got here, all the stuff that’s happened in my life, the whole lot, just reflecting. It’s like bittersweet. It’s going to be nice to get back.

“I was always proud to be Irish.I wanted to do good things and big things but obviously life didn’t go that way for me with all the stuff and all the media, what people think of me you know and the perception they have of me, but I am still so proud to be from Ireland.

“I’m looking forward to getting back home.”

In 2016, an attempt was made on Kinahan’s life at a boxing weigh-in at the Regency Hotel in Dublin.

After that, he left Ireland, first to go to the Costa Del Sol in Spain and later settling in Dubai for the past decade.

The Kinahan cartel was involved in a feud with the rival Hutch crime gang in Ireland, which began in 2015 and resulted in 18 deaths.

A lawyer for Kinahan told the BBC in 2021 that he has no criminal record or convictions and allegations about being a crime boss were false.

News.title: Liverpool vs Monaco LIVE: Team news as Van Dijk and Isak start pre-season friendly at Anfield
News.content:
Why Andoni Iraola Is PERFECT For Liverpool

Andoni Iraola will manage Liverpool at Anfield for the first time as his side welcomes Monaco for their penultimate friendly of pre-season.

Liverpool experienced mixed fortunes in their tour of the United States, which saw them beat Sunderland and Wrexham before enduring a dismal capitulation against Leeds in their final outing, surrendering a two-goal lead in the second half to lose 4-2 to their Premier League rivals.

Iraola will hope to take key lessons from that match into his Anfield bow against the Ligue 1 side, two weeks out from their season opener at Newcastle.

The Spaniard now has almost his full squad at his disposal after the likes of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson Becker and Cody Gakpo returned from their post-World Cup breaks, while new signing Victor Munoz could also be in line for a debut.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

Sports.title: Liverpool given Ronald Araujo transfer update as Hansi Flick makes Barcelona admission
Sports.content:
Liverpool given Ronald Araujo transfer update as Hansi Flick makes Barcelona admission

Ronald Araujo is set to complete his move to Liverpool after the Reds agreed to sign the Barcelona captain on a season-long loan deal with an option to buy

View 2 Images Ronald Araujo of Barcelona is expected to join Liverpool on loan (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Barcelona manager Hansi Flick has confirmed that Ronald Araujo will complete a move to Liverpool. The Reds have been linked with signing a new central defender following the injury to Joe Gomez during pre-season.

‌



News emerged earlier this week that Liverpool had agreed a deal to sign Araujo from Barcelona on a season-long loan, which will also include an option to make the move permanent.

‌



Gomez’s injury has left Liverpool with only one fully-fit senior centre-back in their squad (Virgil van Dijk), while Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni are still recovering from their injury concerns.

‌



Araujo has arrived on to Merseyside on Sunday to undergo a medical to become a Liverpool player.

The 27-year-old has spent the last eight years at Barcelona, racking up 213 appearances and netting 14 goals, and was named as the club's captain in January following the loan exit of Marc-Andre ter Stegen.

Darwin Nunez has given thumbs up to Liverpool transfer as deal gets seal of approval READ MORE :

However, he managed only 16 starts last season and took time away for mental health reasons after facing severe criticism following his red card during the Champions League defeat to Chelsea in November.

‌



Araujo came back in January and lifted the La Liga trophy in May after Barcelona defeated fierce rivals Real Madrid 2-0 at the Camp Nou to secure first place.

However, Flick is allowing his skipper to depart and speaking following his side's friendlies against Nottingham Forest and Udinese on Saturday, he said: "I think Ronald is a great guy and a fantastic player.

"I think our style of play, that we want to play, is a little bit different. He's a player that has a lot of speed, he's physical and very strong and also with the ball he's quite good.

‌



View 2 Images Ronald Araujo is set to join Liverpool on loan from Barcelona. (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"We couldn't include him like I wanted and also I think he wants to make something new. You know it more than me because in the past, something has happened, so this affected him.

‌



"I saw him this morning and I said goodbye and I think he was very happy and Liverpool is also a fantastic club. I wish him all the best because he deserves it.

"He's a fantastic guy and fantastic player and was a great captain."

It's understood the season-long loan features a £47m option for Liverpool to sign rather than an obligation.

‌



The Reds are grappling with several defensive absences as they continue preparations for their Premier League curtain-raiser at Newcastle United on August 23.

At centre-back, Gomez faces several weeks out with a muscle problem sustained in the friendly against Sunderland; new arrival Jacquet is yet to appear as he regains fitness following shoulder surgery; Leoni remains absent from an ACL injury suffered last September, and teenager Ifeanyi Ndukwe is ineligible.

At right-back, Conor Bradley has been unavailable since January following a serious knee injury while Jeremie Frimpong has been dealing with several fitness problems since his move from Bayer Leverkusen last summer. Liverpool host Monaco at Anfield at 2.30pm on Sunday.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho takes 'low level' swipe at Bernardo Silva after Real Madrid debut
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho takes 'low level' swipe at Bernardo Silva after Real Madrid debut

Bernardo Silva made his first appearance for Real Madrid in a pre-season friendly against Ferencvaros on Saturday and Jose Mourinho gave a typically ruthless post-match comment

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho didn't hold back (Image: Real Madrid TV)

Ruthless Jose Mourinho has told Bernardo Silva that he 'has to improve' and criticised the new Real Madrid star's 'low level' of fitness. Silva, 31, joined Mourinho's side on a free transfer after his contract with Manchester City expired in June.

‌



The Portugal international made his debut on Saturday, helping Real beat Hungarian giants Ferencvaros 2-1 in a pre-season friendly. Silva played the second half and gave fans a first glimpse of the 'incredible player' that Mourinho has described him as.

‌



But it was the rest of his manager's comments which raised eyebrows. "He is very important, but the poor guy is one of those players who benefits mentally from not doing anything during vacation, and he arrived for pre-season at a fairly low physical level," Mourinho told Real Madrid TV.

‌



"He has to improve. But he is an incredible player."

The Los Blancos boss then explained how he changed Silva's position during the second half to compensate for his apparent lack of sharpness. "During the game, I realised he was lacking a little physical strength, so I moved him forward to the No. 10 position," Mourinho added.

‌



"He can play there, too. He can play in three or four positions."

In addition to his criticism of Silva, Mourinho commented on Vinicius Junior'sr decision to sign a new six-year contract with Real after crunch talks over his future. Arsenal were waiting in the wings with a lucrative offer, but the Brazilian has opted to extend his stay at the Bernabeu.

‌

"The most important thing is his contract renewal," Mourinho said. "It's a joy for him and for all of us. With so few training sessions, these are players who come into a game with tired legs from training.

"I didn't expect him to run 50 meters with the ball and score. He will surely be better on Wednesday (against Deportivo La Coruna) and even better on Sunday (against Schalke)."

Sports.title: 'The Infantino era is over' - La Liga chief gives damning verdict on FIFA president
Sports.content:
'The Infantino era is over' - La Liga chief gives damning verdict on FIFA president

The FIFA president is coming under fire following failed plans to sell shares in the World Cup and the Club World Cup.

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino is under increasing pressure. (Image: Gabriel Aponte/Getty Images)

The president of the Spanish La Liga, Javier Tebas, has hit out at both Gianni Infantino and FIFA amid growing pressure on the leader of football's governing body. There are calls for him to resign after the failed plans to sell shares in the World Cup.

‌



The plans faced a huge backlash, with UEFA threatening to boycott tournaments should the plans go through. While they have now been scrapped, Infantino has refused to step down from his role, with FIFA claiming he has their 'full support'.

‌



Both the Football Association and the Welsh FA are among those to formally withdraw their support for Infantino ahead of the FIFA elections in March next year. To win the election, he needs the support of 106 of the 211 associations, which looks far from certain.

‌



Diego Simeone confirms Julian Alvarez transfer 'decision' amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

FIFA issues furious response on bid to 'undermine' Gianni Infantino after UEFA admission READ MORE :

La Liga chief Tebas is the latest to speak out against the FIFA president. Speaking to Le Monde he didn't hold back on his thoughts.

"What is happening does not surprise me. What does surprise me is the reaction of many people who remained silent for years," he said.

"This episode is only the tip of the iceberg of what has been going on within an institution, FIFA, but also more broadly in football, where there are no real governance policies. And the problem is not limited to one person: It is about an entire system.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"The old system can persist even when the people change. Let's hope things truly change, that a new leader arrives, and that new governance is established at FIFA."

Speaking specifically about Infantino, he added: "For me, Gianni Infantino's time has long since passed. I'm not saying this because of recent events; I have noticed this style of management for a long time, though everyone else seems to be discovering it only now.

‌



"Look at the organisation of the Club World Cup, what happened in the effort to make it profitable… Decisions were made without key stakeholders in football – the leagues – even being informed. That is how things have been managed for years.

View 2 Images La Liga president Javier Tebas has hit out at Gianni Infantino and FIFA. (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images for Soccerex)

"And I have not forgotten the Super League episode, where Gianni Infantino appeared in the working documents of the league's promoters. In fact, there are connections: Some of the same actors from that time are now involved in the FIFA Forward Enterprise project.

‌



"Gianni Infantino is not someone who contributes to the growth of football. On the contrary, his projects are destroying the very essence of the sport: the national leagues.

"Football is not limited to the elite. For me, the Infantino era is over.

"What remains to be seen is when that will take effect and how the succession will unfold. I hope it is not just a matter of swapping out some people for others, but of a genuine overhaul."

Sports.title: Chelsea flop set for MLS move just two months after Cesc Fabregas punt
Sports.content:
Chelsea flop set for MLS move just two months after Cesc Fabregas punt

Former Chelsea striker Alvaro Morata joined Como on a permanent deal this summer and could join another club before the window closes

View 2 Images Alvaro Morata could be on the move again this summer (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Former Chelsea striker Alvaro Morata could be on the move this summer, despite only signing for a new club on a permanent basis two months ago. Morata joined Serie A outfit Como back in June, having spent last season on loan from AC Milan.

‌



Morata spent three years at Chelsea from 2017-20, and eventually left Stamford Bridge to join Atletico Madrid on a permanent deal, having spent the previous campaign on loan with the La Liga outfit.

‌



The Spain international went on to join Como, who are managed by former Chelsea star Cesc Fabregas, last season on loan from Milan, which included an obligation for the move to become permanent this summer.

‌



Como confirmed earlier this summer that they had completed the signing of Morata on a permanent basis, and now there are reports that the striker could be heading for the exit door at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium.

Arsenal line up £85m Vinicius Jr alternative but immediately hit by transfer issue READ MORE :

Ex-Man Utd star Radek Vitek forced to clear up comments immediately after joining new club READ MORE :

It has been reported by journalist Gianluca Di Marzio that Major League Soccer outfit Atlanta United have expressed an interest in signing Morata this summer.

The report claims that the United States-based club have set their sights on bringing in a striker this summer, with another former Chelsea star, Romelu Lukaku, also said to have been identified as a potential target.

‌



It has been claimed, though, that Lukaku has a preference to join Fenerbahce rather than move across the Atlantic. As a result, it remains to be seen if Atlanta will push on and try to sign Morata.

View 2 Images Alvaro Morata spent three years at Chelsea from 2017-20 (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Morata failed to find the back of the net during his loan spell with Como last season, despite making 26 appearances for the Serie A side, who finished fourth in the table and secured Champions League qualification.

Since leaving Chelsea, Morata has had spells at Atletico Madrid, Juventus, Milan, Galatasaray and Como, and it now remains to be seen if the former Blues star will be on the move yet again this summer.

Sports.title: West Ham have reasons for optimism despite relegation but hard work isn't over
Sports.content:
West Ham have reasons for optimism despite relegation but hard work isn't over

Nuno Espirito Santo is targeting promotion with West Ham but there is still work to do in the lead-up to their Championship opener

View 3 Images There is still reason for hope about West Ham (Image: Getty)

West Ham United might be playing in a lower division than this time last year but there's some optimism around the London Stadium. However, a lack of summer signings means some concerns remain.

‌



Positivity is a strange feeling given the pain of relegation in May. And yet there are reasons to be cheerful - not least Jarrod Bowen's decision to stay.

‌



Club captain Bowen narrowly missed out on a place in Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad and was linked with an instant Premier League return. But the former Hull City forward was convinced to stay and lead a promotion charge after meeting with Hammers chiefs.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"I did an interview after [the final game of last season] and said my vision is to get this club back in the Premier League," Bowen said in July when announcing he was staying. "Sometimes you think it falls on deaf ears and people say 'he's just saying that'.

"But when I say something, I don't hide away from it. It was a no-brainer for me to be here and the vision is clear, it's the Premier League."

‌



View 3 Images Nuno has agreed to stay on as manager (Image: PA)

The last time Bowen was in the Championship, he was the seventh-highest scorer in the division despite leaving Hull for West Ham mid-season. And he isn't the only one hoping to call upon expertise at this level to lead the Hammers back up at the first time of asking.

Nuno Espirito Santo couldn't keep the team in the top flight, though there was a notable improvement after he was allowed to bring in some of his own signings in January. The Portuguese coach has already won the Championship once before, albeit nearly a decade ago with Wolves, and is ready to target another title.

‌



There has been some uncertainty behind the scenes, with joint-chair David Sullivan stepping down and a consortium including Amanda Staveley now looking to take a stake in the club. But the Hammers have insisted this won't affect day-to-day affairs.

West Ham know they will be there to be got at, though, and need to keep their focus. Experience at this level can help, with Kyle Walker-Peters and Mads Hermansen both earning promotion to the Premier League in recent years.

‌



"The other teams will make it difficult for us, but we just have to focus on ourselves, do our work and be confident," said full-back Walker-Peters, who came up with Southampton in 2024.

Nuno's decision to stay could well be a factor in convincing important players to follow suit. Taty Castellanos joined from Lazio for £25m and scored six goals in 18 games, but has been a fixture in pre-season and there's still hope he stays put.

Efforts are also being made to keep hold of last season's Hammer of the Year, Dinos Mavropanos, despite Premier League interest. There is even faint hope that Axel Disasi, so impressive on loan last season, can be convinced to drop down a division.

‌



View 3 Images West Ham have lost key players like Fernandes (Image: Getty)

Of course, there have been some sales which naturally follow a drop down to the second tier. The departure of academy graduate Freddie Potts hasn't gone down well with everyone. But bringing in well above £100m for Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville should mean the club can be more selective when it comes to future sales.

Callum Wilson and Adama Traore have left for free and other high earners such as Jean-Clair Todibo and Niclas Fullkrug could also soon leave. Then there's the lack of new faces. Keiber Lamadrid - on loan last season but used just once by Nuno - was the only senior signing as July ticked into August, though Joel Veltman has since followed.

Still, it's worth remembering this is a squad which picked up 39 points in the Premier League last season and gave title-winners Arsenal a real fright in May. The challenge now is to rebuild with Bowen at the core and time is running out to get the necessary deals over the line.

Sports.title: Man Utd, Arsenal and Chelsea target who had £87m release clause is now a free agent
Sports.content:
Man Utd, Arsenal and Chelsea target who had £87m release clause is now a free agent

A striker who was once one of European football's hottest goalscoring properties has seen his stock plummet in recent years

View 2 Images Andrea Belotti has endured a difficult few years (Image: Getty)

At the peak of his powers, Italy international Andrea Belotti was one of the world's most in-demand strikers. These days, though, the former Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea target is available for free.

‌



Belotti was a relatively late bloomer, only making his Serie A debut at the age of 20 with Palermo. He left for Torino in 2015, and it was there that he made a name for himself.

‌



He scored a career-best 26 Serie A goals in 2016/17, narrowly missing out on the Capocannoniere award to Edin Dzeko. He signed a contract extension midway through that season, with Torino including a €100m (£87m) release clause.

‌



That clause was only applicable to clubs outside Italy. However, club president Urbano Cairo publicly admitted his fears that it might not be high enough to stave off Premier League interest, as United, Arsenal and Chelsea, among others, were sniffing around.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club READ MORE :

Jadon Sancho's Man Utd decline and manager trend leaves unwanted star in awkward spot READ MORE :

"When I included a €100million release clause in Belotti's contract somebody thought it was an excessive fee, now they think it's not enough," Cairo told Tuttosport in 2017. "I think nobody will come here to trigger his release clause and it would be better for him to stay for one more season at Torino.

‌



View 2 Images Belotti's Torino form attracted plenty of suitors (Image: Getty)

"I've read he's happy here and I'll need to talk to him. He can still improve, play one more season for us, play the [2018] World Cup and then we'll see."

Belotti scored four times in World Cup qualifying but drew a blank as the Azzurri lost a play-off against Sweden to miss out on the tournament. Torino didn't have to worry about anyone meeting his release clause, though, with the striker himself suggesting he wasn't worth that much.

‌



"To be honest, no [I don't feel I am worth it]," Belotti told Mediaset in April 2017. "But given the way the transfer market has developed, increasingly ridiculous sums are being spent. The cost of players has gone up far too much."

But his focus wasn't dented. He hit double figures in each of his first six Torino seasons and was part of the Italy squad which won Euro 2020. When he left his club in 2022, he did so with exactly 100 league goals under his belt.

Things have been much tougher in the years since. He failed to score a single league goal in his first season at Roma and has just 22 goals across more than 140 games in all competitions for four different clubs in Italy and Portugal.

‌

Now 32, he spent last season at Cagliari but was limited to eight appearances after a serious knee injury. According to reports in Italy, he was poised to rejoin the Sardinian club only to fail a medical.

His international career is very much in the rear-view window, with no caps since June 2022. That £87m release clause feels like a distant memory.

Sports.title: Arsenal's champion squad will leave Mikel Arteta having to digest harsh reality
Sports.content:
Arsenal's champion squad will leave Mikel Arteta having to digest harsh reality

Arsenal have confirmed the signing of Bruno Guimaraes as their star-studded squad gets even stronger - leaving Mikel Arteta the unenviable task of keeping all his players happy

View 4 Images Arsenal have added even more quality by signing Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal finally got their man on Saturday as they paraded the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes - adding more quality to an already champion side.

‌



Mikel Arteta is certainly making sure he doesn't rest on his laurels and Arsenal are striking whilst the knife is hot. They've already spent north of £100million on their squad as they seek to remain top of the pile ahead of the new season kicking off.

‌



Arsenal have very much been a coming force in recent years. The only question mark over them becoming champions and ending their Premier League drought was a mental one. The quality they had assembled over the years meant winning silverware was looking a matter of when, not if.

‌



The building of such a team saw renowned Gunners fan Piers Morgan claim that they had assembled the greatest squad in the history of world football. His bold statement wasn't met with widespread agreement, but it serves to underline just how impressive the group they've assembled is.

Arsenal line up £85m Vinicius Jr alternative but immediately hit by transfer issue READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes reveals private Declan Rice message after sealing Arsenal transfer READ MORE :

Arsenal can certainly ride this wave, which they inevitably will in the 12 months after becoming champions. They're favourites to retain their crown, and becoming back-to-back champions would give them even more pull, but players fundamentally want to play.

This star-studded squad they now boast began being properly assembled in the summer of 2021, just before they started mixing it in the European picture after several below par years. They signed the likes of Ben White and Martin Odegaard and every summer since they added serious quality, breaking their club-record fee along the way.

‌



Their team, and its depth, now is akin to the squad Jose Mourinho's Chelsea had in the early Roman Abramovich days, or the quality Pep Guardiola could boast in his Manchester City heyday.

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta can currently boast immense depth at Arsenal (Image: Getty)

Those two elite managers eventually had to stomach letting players depart whom they will have wanted to keep, but there's only so many starting spots available each week. Mourinho had to let the likes of Arjen Robben, Tiago, Scott Parker and Glen Johnson leave - all of whom enjoyed impressive spells post-Chelsea.

‌



Guardiola waved off Julian Alvarez, Cole Palmer and Ferran Torres. The overriding reason every time was that the player simply didn't want to settle for a squad role.

Arteta spoke about enlarging the bench numbers back in January as he addressed the difficulty of constantly leaving summer signing Christian Norgaard out of his match squads. It did came across with an element of self loathing - I'm sure Arteta, with the riches available to him, wanted to have a host of £50m signings to change the game from the bench.

View 4 Images Julian Alvarez left Man City after refusing to accept a back-up role (Image: Getty)

‌



Shame, not every club can have a squad so luxurious, and so limiting the bench numbers serves as some kind of an equaliser. Equally don't sign a player, that was only ever signed as cover, and they bemoan his lack of involvement.

"At the moment there are two or three players who have to be out of the squad. That's a reality and I cannot change that." he said earlier this year. "These are the rules. Hopefully the Premier League next season instead of 18 outfield players they will do 20.

"I beg them from here, [have it] like it is in the Champions League, because it's much better to manage the squad, to maintain the value of the players, to maintain the mental health of the players as nobody wants to get out of the squad. I beg them to help us with that. We can deal with hotels, travel and all of that. That would be very, very helpful for all of us. The worst thing is to leave somebody."

‌



Rather than giving Arsenal the scope to have a bigger bench, the reality is Arteta is going to have to decide who he is going to hang his hat on, and who he can afford to lose. Certain players may take that out of his hand if they seek to take greater control of their career.

View 4 Images Max Dowman, Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze are among those eyeing spots in Arsenal's starting side next season

You only need to look at the numbers. A graphic showing Arsenal's depth will highlight that the Gunners have close to three players for every midfield and attacking position.

‌



Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Odegaard and now Guimaraes all want a midfield spot. Arsenal play two wingers every game - and Arteta needs to pick from Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Martinelli, Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze. They've just added Christos Tzolis and remain in the market for another blockbuster name after missing out on Vinicius Junior. This is before accounting for academy stars Ethan Nwaneri, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Max Dowman.

There's no doubt Arsenal have a squad that nearly every club in Europe would envy, but such depth has a short lifespan. Guardiola constantly spoke about needing to streamline his squad because players who don't play become unhappy, and that impacts on the environment. This is a reality Arteta may have to face sooner rather than later.

Sports.title: Five-time Super League winner Makinson to retire at end of 2026 campaign
Sports.content:
Tommy Makinson has announced he will retire from rugby league at the end of the current 2026 Super League campaign.

The Catalans Dragons wing, 34, spent the majority of his career with St Helens between 2011 and 2024, winning five Super League titles in 2014, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022 and making more than 300 appearances.

Makinson also won a World Club Challenge, a Challenge Cup and four League Leaders' Shields with Saints, and was selected in the Super League Dream Team on three occasions.

A prolific try scorer, Makinson scored over 200 tries for St Helens and has since notched 20 tries in 37 appearances for Catalans after joining the club ahead of the 2025 season. He also represented England over 20 times.

"As the 2026 season moves towards its final stages, I feel now is the right time to announce that this will be my final season as a professional rugby league player," Makinson posted on Instagram.

Image: Makinson played for St Helens between 2011 and 2024, winning five Super League titles

"Rugby league has been incredibly kind to me, and when I look back on the journey I've been on, I feel nothing but pride and gratitude. I've been very fortunate to live out a dream I had as a kid and represent some of the biggest clubs both in England and France and also the pinnacle which is representing my country.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Makinson score a special try for St Helens with millimetres to work with against Leigh Leopards

"There have been so many highs, some difficult moments, incredible memories and friendships that will last a lifetime. I wouldn't have been able to experience any of it without the unbelievable support I've had from my family, friends, team-mates, coaches, staff, supporters and everyone who has played a part in my career. To each and every one of you, thank you.

"I've still got a few games left, and I want to enjoy every second of them. I'll be taking it all in, appreciating the moments and giving everything I have to finish this chapter of my career in the best possible way.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Makinson makes acrobatic pass to Reimis Smith who goes over for an impressive Catalans Dragons try against Hull FC

"It's hard to put into words what rugby league has given me, but I know how lucky I am to have lived this life and played the game I love for as long as I have."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Thorslund ends Johnson's undisputed run to become world champion again
Sports.content:
Dina Thorslund is a world champion again after ending Cherneka Johnson's undisputed run to cap an emotional return to the sport.

Just over a year after vacating her WBC and WBO bantamweight titles because she was pregnant, the undefeated Thorslund fought aggressively from the start to snatch the WBC, WBO, WBA and IBF titles from Johnson, winning every round in a unanimous decision in the main event of MVPW-5 in Orlando, Florida.

Thorslund (25-0, nine KOs) vacated her titles in June 2025, and a month later she announced on social media that she had suffered a miscarriage.

She returned to the ring in January and defeated Almudena Alvarez to capture the vacant WBC interim featherweight title. Then Thorslund, who is 32 years old and from Denmark, dropped back to bantamweight to fight for the undisputed championship.

The lead-up to Saturday's fight brought more emotional turmoil for Thorslund, whose training partner, Raven Chapman, underwent emergency brain surgery last month after she collapsed during a sparring session in Denmark.

"This has been such an emotional journey for me the last year," Thorslund said, fighting back tears.

"I'm going to take this [title belt] straight back to Raven and say thank you."

Image: Johnson (left) and Thorslund finally met in the headline act of MVPW-05 in Orlando

Thorslund was in control for the whole fight. Her aggressive combinations put Johnson on the defensive, especially early, and through three rounds, Thorslund had landed 37 punches to Johnson's 14. In the end, Thorslund's non-stop attack of power punches built a 103-62 edge. All three judges scored it 100-90.

Johnson (19-3, eight KOs), who became undisputed champion by knocking out Shurretta Metcalf in July 2025, was unable to utilise her power against Thorslund. Practically every time she connected, Thorslund would respond by landing three or four shots in return.

Sports.title: In-form Norrie defeated in Montreal while Sabalenka suffers shock loss
Sports.content:
Britain's Cameron Norrie has been knocked out of the National Bank Open at the last-16 stage following a 6-2 7-6 (10-8) defeat by Arthur Fils in Montreal.

The French 18th seed looked dominant early on in the Montreal contest, utilising his powerful serve well to wrap up the first set without much hassle.

Norrie stepped up a gear in the second, matching Fils' power to force a tie-break.

Despite creating two set-point opportunities, Norrie was ultimately unable to convert when it mattered and Fils sealed the win in one hour and 43 minutes.

Norrie knocked out third seed Alex de Minaur in the round prior, turning the tables from match-point down by winning 11 out of the next 13 games to beat the Australian 5-7 7-6 (7-5) 6-1 - a victory that saw him become British No 1 again in place of Arthur Fery - but he was unable to build on that win.

Sabalenka suffers US Open build-up setback

World No 1 Aryna Sabalenka suffered a setback in her US ‌Open build-up when she was beaten 7-6 (7-3) 4-6 6-4 by Russia's Ekaterina Alexandrova in ‌the fourth round of the Canadian Open in Toronto.

The 16th-seeded ​Alexandrova fought a hard battle lasting nearly two-and-a-half hours to secure her quarter-final ​berth.

Sabalenka, a four-time Grand Slam champion and ‌reigning US Open winner, recovered from a set down to force a ​decider but was unable to halt Alexandrova's aggressive shot-making in the final set.

Image: Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shock Canadian Open loss against Ekaterina Alexandrova at the last-16 stage

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the National Bank Open match between Sabalenka and Alexandrova

The Belarusian broke early in the opening set ​before Alexandrova rallied to force a tie-break, ⁠which the Russian won to ⁠move ahead.

Sabalenka responded by seizing control of the second set with a break for a ‌4-3 lead before serving out to level the match.

Alexandrova held her nerve in the decider as Sabalenka's error count rose. ‌Serving to stay in the match at 4-5, the top seed saved two match points, but a double fault on the third handed victory to the Russian.

"I just tried to play ⁠every single point as if it was ​the last one because with her, you don't [get] ​a lot of chances during the match," Alexandrova ​said in her on-court interview.

"Honestly, I was trying not ⁠to think about the score or anything. Just hit the ball, and that's it.

Sports.title: McKenna vows middleweight domination as heir to Golovkin and Canelo
Sports.content:
New world champion Aaron McKenna is just getting started.

He secured the IBF middleweight title with a victory over Etinosa Oliha on memorable night at the 3Arena in Dublin.

Now he wants to take on the mantle of Canelo Alvarez and Gennadiy Golovkin by dominating the middleweight division.

He is targeting other champions. Denzel Bentley holds the WBO title, Carlos Adames the WBC and Erislandy Lara the WBA. McKenna is calling for all the top 160-pounders to fight one another.

"It doesn't matter [who's next], whoever wants it. I'm easy to find now, I have a belt. There's no hiding any more. I want to collect every single belt in boxing. I'm the best middleweight and super-middleweight in the world. I don't mind jumping up," he told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive the heart-warming moment that saw Stevie McKenna watch his brother Aaron win the IBF world middleweight title

"I've been thinking about this moment since I was six years old. It just goes to show, don't give up, always stay true to yourself. You can do anything."

His ambitions extend far. "The middleweight division's there to be took over. It's been dying for years since GGG (Golovkin) and Canelo left it. I said it again, a year ago, I think I'm going to be the man to take it over," McKenna declared at his post-fight press conference.

"No one really believed me. Until you put in performances like that and then they start listening. In life you've got to prove yourself sometimes. Tonight I've done that. I just hope one of the other world champions will take on the fight so we can clean up this mess of a division."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Aaron McKenna's IBF middleweight world title fight against Etinosa Oliha

He promises he will not shy away from any challenge.

"Anyone. I've said it before and I'll say it again I will literally fight anyone out there. I just want to unify, whatever it takes, prove I'm the best in the world. That's the sport of boxing. You look back in the day, the 80s and 90s, they all fought each other," McKenna said.

"And this is exactly why Zuffa Boxing's going to be the future. It's already taking over. Everybody's fighting each other, there's no more hiding."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna had an incredible entrance ahead of his fight with Oliha, first coming into Sinead O'Connor's The Foggy Dew and then Faithless' Insomnia!

For the time being, he can enjoy his accomplishment.

"Twenty-one years in the making," he concluded. "I don't know how long this is going to take for this to seep in that this has finally happened that I've become world champion. I've been dreaming of this.

"For it to happen now, honestly it's literally unbelievable. I can't describe it."
